arxiv-2603-15148: Bekbaev clarifies the classification of two-dimensional algebras over an arbitrary base field. Such algebras are small, but their full sorting into types had gaps and confusion. His clarification settles how the classes are defined and related. From it, he counts exactly how many non-isomorphic two-dimensional algebras exist over a finite field. The count turns the clarified classification into a concrete number.
arxiv-2603-15348: Zhang and co-authors present ODIS, a spectral imaging system that keeps nearly all incoming light. Coded apertures and beam splitters block much of the light and hurt dim scenes. ODIS slides a disperser along the axis to capture a plain image and a dispersed one on a single path. A deep unfolding network rebuilds the spectrum, guided by the plain image. A deformable convolution module fixes sub-pixel spectral shifts. Benchmarks show state-of-the-art results, with clear gains under low light. A hardware prototype confirms the design.
arxiv-2603-15548: Engh shows that rational inattention can be viewed as a nested regularized optimal transport problem. With entropic optimal transport tools, he recovers the main results of two landmark papers in the area. Matejka and McKay's work and Caplin, Dean, and Leahy's work both fall out of the same frame. The transport view then extends those results beyond their original settings. Arbitrary choice sets are covered, which broadens the reach of the theory.
arxiv-2603-16348: Chakraborty and Steghöfer argue that AI coding prompts are really requirements in disguise. Prompts blend user needs with hints about the solution. A known model splits prompt content into three dimensions. These cover function and quality, general solutions, and specific solutions. The authors state four hypotheses about how prompts evolve. User traits, validation work, and software quality all enter the picture. They sketch a research agenda using real development data and experiments.
arxiv-2603-16448: Jian and co-authors teach SQL agents to work with unknown database schemas. Real company databases hold hundreds of noisy tables. Loading the full schema upfront fails at that scale. Their TRUST-SQL agent finds and verifies just the needed tables. A four-phase protocol grounds each step in checked metadata. A dual-track training strategy splits exploration rewards from execution outcomes. This yields a 9.9% relative gain over standard GRPO. Gains over base models averaged 30.6% and 16.6% for the two model sizes.
arxiv-2603-16648: Marijnissen and co-authors merge dynamic programming with constraint propagation. Two solver styles dominate hard combinatorial problems. State-based search and constraint-based models rarely mix. Their solver prunes DP states and transitions using propagation. A general CP solver supplies the pruning inside the DIDP frame. Tests cover scheduling and routing problems with time windows. Propagation cut state expansions sharply. The combined solver beat a plain DP solver on two problem families.
arxiv-2603-16848: Don-Yehiya and co-authors ask how the anchor model shapes benchmarks that use a language model as judge. Popular benchmarks compare every model against one anchor to save cost. The team tests 22 anchors on the Arena-Hard v2 dataset. They find anchor choice is critical: a poor anchor can sharply cut agreement with human rankings. The best and worst models make poor anchors, since they seldom reveal relative order. The effect size rivals the choice of judge model. They add anchor picking rules from a power analysis.
arxiv-2603-17248: Youssef and Singla present a method to rebuild a full 12 lead ECG from a reduced lead set, tuned to the patient's pathology. Rebuilding is ill posed because bodies vary. Standard deep methods ignore the underlying heart condition and lose vital waveform detail. Their framework aligns latent features with clinical labels through supervised contrastive learning across views. This filters out anatomical nuisance factors. On the PTB-XL dataset, they report about a 76 percent cut in reconstruction error versus the prior best model.
arxiv-2603-17348: Dai and co-authors study the one-dimensional compressible Euler equations with friction and random forcing. They prove that bounded martingale solutions exist for all time and meet an entropy rule. Over time the solutions settle to a constant steady state, and they do so fast. The density then looks like flow through a porous medium, while momentum follows Darcy's law. Sharp entropy estimates drive the proof, they note.
arxiv-2603-17548: Marasco, Evangelista, Piccolomini, and Colajanni present CLeAN, an adaptive normalization method for continual learning on tabular data. Standard scaling needs the whole dataset at once, which streaming tasks never offer. CLeAN learns global feature scales and updates them with an exponential moving average. Tests span two datasets and replay, A-GEM, and EWC strategies. Scores on new data rose while forgetting dropped, they report. Normalization itself guards old knowledge, they argue.
arxiv-2603-17748: Zhang and co-authors study photonic meta-atoms, solitary waves that act like soft-core atoms inside nonlinear waveguides. Atomic physics ideas then describe their level spectra and dynamics. Higher-order dispersion sets sharp resonances that mark each meta-atom, they show. Small changes in the level spectrum shift those resonances. The shifts split into isotopic and isomeric parts that a simple model separates. A generic mechanism adds a Zeeman-like splitting of the lines.
arxiv-2603-17848: Schwede proves a splitting result in Real-global equivariant homotopy theory. The theorem refines the Segal-Becker splitting and the Boltje-Symonds Brauer induction at once. A map from a classifying spectrum to Real-global K-theory gains a section on loop spaces, he shows. That one fact yields the classic splittings on cohomology theories. It also yields explicit Brauer induction on homotopy groups. Adams operations in Real K-theory then rigidify to global self-maps.
arxiv-2603-18048: Xiong and co-authors present DEAF, a bench that tests whether audio language models truly hear sound. It holds over 2,700 conflict items across prosody, background sounds, and speaker identity. Test levels raise text influence step by step, from content clashes to misleading prompts. New metrics measure how much models lean on text over sound. Seven audio models show a clear pattern: text drives most calls, despite real sound sensitivity.
arxiv-2603-18348: Mubashar and Cuzzolin build GANs that track their own doubt with Dempster-Shafer evidence rules. GANs tend to make near-copy samples and lack range in what they produce. Their loss applies evidence rules to both the maker net and the judge net. The maker also outputs a mass value for each pixel of the image. That score lets the model state its doubt and use it to make samples with more range.
arxiv-2603-18448: Liu and co-authors seek universal solutions for shot language understanding in film analysis. Vision-language models disagree with film experts on shot tasks across many cinematographic dimensions. Their SLU-SUITE holds 490K human-annotated question pairs across 33 tasks and six dimensions. Diagnostics expose model bottlenecks and cross-task influences in the data. UniShot, a balanced generalist, and AgentShots, a routed expert cluster, beat task ensembles and lead commercial models by 22% out of domain.
arxiv-2603-18848: Wiebusch describes a simple full-duplex digital link that runs over one coaxial cable. Lab instruments often need modest bandwidth without complex circuits. A passive resistive hybrid gives line matching and direction split. One logic gate drives the line, and a differential receiver acts as comparator. No modulation, transformers, or echo cancellation are used. The design target is 200 megabits per second over ten meters of RG-178 cable. Tests match the predicted timing jitter, staying under 1.2 nanoseconds peak to peak. An open line end even gives free loopback behavior.
arxiv-2603-18948: Ge and co-authors improve a long-standing guess by Erdos and Kleitman on large set families with no matching of a set size. For decades, the best broad lower bound stayed at a plain half of all sets. A 2018 result pushed the bound higher with two elegant proofs. Their new bound edges a bit higher still. The gain comes from a link to a classic result on how Boolean functions respond to input flips. A weaker gain also comes from linear algebra with a twist.
arxiv-2603-19348: Wietrzykowski probes whether all layers of a small transformer do equal work. He tests the 30-layer SmolLM2 model with five diagnostic checks on its weights. Layer weights show strong math order, yet swapped-in predicted weights break the model badly. Layer importance spans a huge range across the depth of the network. A core band of layers is vital, while two layers hurt when kept. Training that funds layers by importance cuts cost by about half. A trial run posts 4.7 times lower loss at the same size.
arxiv-2603-19448: Jensen and co-authors design pulse sequences for dynamic nuclear polarization right on the instrument itself. Pulsed DNP can boost NMR and MRI sensitivity by orders of magnitude. Big spin systems and flawed hardware make pure theory design hard. Their method pairs Bayesian learning with a constrained random walk over pulses. The spectrometer and the real spin sample guide each design step. For trityl and nitroxide samples, wide-band sequences emerge that work in practice. Results are checked against in-silico designs of the same task.
arxiv-2603-19648: Chandak and co-authors analyse stochastic approximation under heavy-tailed and long-range dependent noise. The method is a core iterative tool in reinforcement learning and optimization. Classic theory assumes tame noise with bounded variance. Finance and communications often break that assumption. The team seeks the root of a strongly monotone operator under the rougher noise. They prove the first finite-time moment bounds in both settings. Rates show how heavy tails and long memory slow convergence. Tests on gradient descent support the bounds.
arxiv-2603-19848: Gehér and co-authors study unit distance graphs that allow few crossings per edge. Each edge is a unit segment, and at most k edges may cross it. They ask how many edges such a graph on n points can have. For one crossing per edge, they improve the best known upper bound. The new bound is tight apart from the constant term. For two crossings, they prove the first strong upper bound. They also give a construction that beats the crossing-free case.
arxiv-2603-19948: Riso and co-authors present a coupled cluster method for positron binding in molecules and anions. Their POS-CCSD method treats electrons and the positron on an equal footing. It includes excitations up to two electrons plus one positron at once. They test it on atomic anions and several polar and nonpolar molecules. For the hydrogen anion, converged results match Monte Carlo and other strong methods well. Full match with experiments is not reached, due to slow convergence with basis size.
arxiv-2603-20048: Naoumi, Bennis, and Chafii learn structured latent dynamics for wireless channel data. Their self supervised frame treats channel state paths as a world modeling task. A joint embedding design learns action linked dynamics in a compact latent space. Transitions use updates drawn from Lie algebra. This choice keeps the latent space well shaped as scenes change. On the DICHASUS dataset, the method beat strong baselines at keeping topology. It also forecast future embeddings better in unseen environments. The charts it makes could aid scheduling and localization.
arxiv-2603-20748: Lau widens the gap between quantum and classical play in a nonlocal game. The magic square game held the best known gap of one ninth. That score used two Bell states with a perfect quantum plan. A claimed larger gap for the doily game rests on one hidden premise. Lau shows that dropping it cuts the gap back to one ninth. He then builds a new game with a gap of four thirty fifths. This beats the old mark and resets the record.
arxiv-2603-20948: Almeida and co-authors present gUFO, a light version of the Unified Foundational Ontology for the Semantic Web. UFO is a mature ontology used in many research and industry projects, and it is now in ISO standardization. gUFO targets OWL 2 DL knowledge graphs. It stands out for its typology of types, which puts OntoClean guidelines into practice. It also offers patterns for intrinsic and relational aspects, situations, and higher order types. They compare it with BFO and DOLCE based versions.
arxiv-2603-21148: Krauthgamer and Petruschka build a fast nearest neighbor data structure for lp spaces with p above two. Nearest neighbor search must preprocess a point set so queries return the closest point quickly. They focus on the fast query time regime that large online systems need. Their randomized structure gives an approximation factor that grows mildly with p. It uses polynomial space in dimension and point count. The result improves on, or is incomparable to, the best prior work in this regime.
arxiv-2603-21248: Kyaw and co-authors use large language models to fuse knowledge graphs across languages. Merging graphs across languages is hard due to semantic differences and graph complexity. Their framework turns triples into plain language sequences. The model then maps relations and reconciles entities between a growing fused graph and each new candidate graph. On the DBP15K data set, graphs merge one by one into a coherent whole. The design is modular and suits ongoing knowledge synthesis from many sources.
arxiv-2603-21448: Spera proposes a new design for task-oriented dialogue systems, where safety checks double as a way to reuse answers. Systems today recompute each turn from scratch, even when the answer follows from earlier state. In capability-based systems, the safety certification step already computes a closure of all reachable answers. Spera's Certified Answer Store saves those answers with small provenance witnesses at each certified turn. Later queries then resolve in under a millisecond through formal containment checks, with no fresh retrieval or generation.
arxiv-2603-21548: Abaei and co-authors review a one-year software engineering internship program at RMIT University in Melbourne. Year-long placements give students deep industry contact and help close gaps between study and work. The authors trace how the course changed over ten years to meet student needs. From 91 internship reports in 2023 and 2024, they draw out three challenge themes students faced. They also note which courses students found most useful on placement. Their recommendations target educators and host companies that want interns to learn more.
arxiv-2603-22148: Zhao and co-authors present OpenEarth-Agent, an agent for Earth observation in open settings. Older remote sensing agents call fixed tools, so they fail on new data and new tasks. This agent plans its workflow and creates the tools it needs instead. It draws on multi-stage tools and cross-domain knowledge bases. The team also builds OpenEarth-Bench, with 596 full real-world cases in seven domains. Tests show the agent runs full pipelines across domains. With six base models, it matches agents that rely on 104 set tools.
arxiv-2603-22248: Cai and Li give the first theory for confidence-based decoding in diffusion language models. Such models unmask many tokens per step, in any order. Which tokens to unmask, and how many, sets the sampling speed. Confidence-based rules pick tokens by prediction confidence and work well in practice. The authors study an entropy-sum rule. It keeps unmasking until total entropy passes a set threshold. They prove it samples near-exactly with few iterations when data entropy is low. The rule adapts to data with no tuning.
arxiv-2603-22348: Hu and co-authors present COMPASS-Hedge, an online learner that stays safe without knowing the setting. Online methods face a three-way tension. They want low regret in both foe and calm settings, plus baseline safety. Past methods hit at most two of the three without oracle tuning. COMPASS-Hedge hits all three at once, up to log factors. It needs no prior knowledge of gaps. The design mixes adaptive pseudo-regret scaling with phase-based aggression. A comparator-aware mixing step keeps the baseline promise.
arxiv-2603-22648: Xie, Guo, and Xu present AwesomeLit, a visual system that helps new researchers work through the literature. Finding gaps and forming a testable idea are hard for beginners. General deep research tools are not built for that task, and language models can hallucinate. AwesomeLit offers a clear, user-steered agent workflow. It also shows a query tree with sources and a map of how papers relate. A small study with early researchers found the tool helped them explore new topics. Users also found promising directions and gained confidence in results.
arxiv-2603-22748: Naganuma and Kitagawa test a magnetic compound first flagged by an AI model. The compound, MnFeCo4Si2, came from Google DeepMind's GNoME system. It has a layered-like structure. The authors confirm it forms a single-phase rhombohedral crystal, as predicted. They measure its magnetic behavior in the lab. The compound proves to be a soft ferromagnet. Its Curie temperature is 1039 kelvin. The work serves as a lab check on AI-driven materials discovery.
arxiv-2603-22948: Gudmundsson, Sha, and Wong give linear-time shortest path algorithms for Euclidean graph classes. A classic result covers planar graphs, but it does not extend to Euclidean classes. The authors set criteria that a Euclidean graph class must meet. Any class meeting them admits a linear-time single-source shortest path method, they prove. A key step shows contracted graphs of these classes have small separators. That separator result powers the fast algorithm.
arxiv-2603-23348: Moretti and three co-authors study k-center clustering when the dataset keeps changing. Points arrive over time and go stale, so clusters must track the live set. Past work used sliding windows or fully dynamic updates with no warning. Their new setting gives each point a known lifetime at arrival. They build a deterministic algorithm with a 2 plus epsilon approximation. Its update time stays near k over epsilon, and memory grows with the live points. A second algorithm trades a looser factor for sublinear memory on tame inputs.
arxiv-2603-23448: Zhang and five co-authors build c-CRAB, a benchmark that grades AI code review agents. Code-writing agents now flood projects with pull requests, so review quality matters more. The dataset grows out of real human reviews of pull requests. Each human review spawns tests that check what an agent's review catches. Four leading review agents together solve only about 40% of the tasks. Agent reviews also stress different points than human reviews do. The authors see room for human-agent teamwork in future review practice.
arxiv-2603-23948: Chen and co-authors simulate thermalization in an SU(2) lattice gauge theory on IBM quantum computers. They use linear plaquette chains with up to 151 plaquettes. They track the entanglement spectrum, Rényi-2 entropy, and anti-flatness on small subsystems over time. After error mitigation, hardware results match extrapolated classical results for chains up to 101 plaquettes. Their work shows that local thermalization in chaotic quantum systems can be studied on current noisy quantum hardware.
arxiv-2603-24148: Hayakawa and Takada give an exactly solvable model of the Mpemba effect in two dimensions. The Mpemba effect is when a hotter system can cool faster than a cooler one. Their model is an overdamped Langevin system in a round, bistable potential built from quadratic and log pieces. That shape maps the Fokker-Planck operator to a Schrödinger-type problem with analytic modes. They derive mode amplitudes for long-time relaxation. The slowest mode varies non-monotonically with starting temperature, and they state a crossing condition for the effect.
arxiv-2603-24548: Kalyabin finds a sharp unconditional link between two number-theoretic quantities. On one side is the remainder in a modified Mertens formula for sums of prime reciprocals. On the other is the maximal value of Gronwall numbers among integers whose greatest prime factor is a given prime p, restricted to integers divisible by some smaller prime. As p grows, a sharp limit relationship between the two is established, with no assumption of the Riemann hypothesis. The proofs rest on properties of Gronwall numbers from the author's earlier preprints.
arxiv-2603-24648: Omeke and co-authors design an energy-efficient federated anomaly detection system for underwater networks. Underwater acoustic links are slow, costly in energy, and often cannot reach the surface gateway. Their three-tier framework pairs sensors with nearby fog nodes in a feasibility-aware way. Model updates are compressed before sending, and fog nodes cooperate selectively, exchanging only when small clusters gain from larger neighbours. A physics-based acoustic model scores detection quality, energy use, and participation. In a 200-sensor test, only 48 percent could reach the gateway.
arxiv-2603-24748: Poghosyan and co-authors design a distributed MPC scheme for coordinated path-following for vehicles. The framework they build on decouples space and time, so the joint task shrinks to a one-dimensional one. Their scheme handles the time layer. Using the normalised Laplacian, they split the dynamics into independent modes. A recursion links current and predicted states. For a horizon of one step on a fixed connected network, the system is exponentially stable despite path errors. The form also admits mission limits and collision avoidance.
arxiv-2603-24948: Zhou and co-authors develop a latent-space method for correcting PDE models and quantifying uncertainty. When governing physics is misspecified, learned models need correction, and parameter-space sampling can be costly. Their framework extends a latent-variable Gaussian process solver. A shared confidence-aware encoder builds a stochastic latent representation against a Gaussian process prior. Two decoders then predict the solution distribution and a discrepancy term that absorbs model-form error. Both decoders quantify uncertainty jointly, under soft physics constraints and noisy data.
arxiv-2603-25048: Hu and co-authors automate solver setup for hardware model checking with AutoPDR. The PDR algorithm proves circuit safety, but its speed swings wildly with parameter choices. Hand tuning is slow and needs expert skill, while generic tuners waste time a proof task cannot spare. AutoPDR learns from circuit graphs plus traits of structure and wiring. It predicts a good setup for each circuit. Expert rules first drop bad options, cutting the search space by 78 percent. On a benchmark suite, the picked setups beat default and common settings.
arxiv-2603-25248: Patel and Dutta add attention weights to a late-interaction search method. ColBERT-style search scores each query word against document words late in the pipe, which is fast and sharp. But it ignores how much each word mattered inside the model. ColBERT-Att folds those attention weights into the match scores. The change aims to weigh key word pairs more than filler pairs. Recall improves on MS-MARCO. Gains also show across wide BEIR and LoTTE test sets.
arxiv-2603-25448: Basak and co-authors study the first nonzero Steklov-Neumann eigenvalue on ring-shaped domains. The domain is one ball with a smaller ball cut out. Among such rings with fixed radii, they show the eigenvalue peaks when the balls sit dead center. Bounds follow for star-shaped rings on curved sheets with a spin-symmetric metric. They also track the value as the hole shrinks toward a point. The nodal pattern of the matching eigenfunction gets a count as well.
arxiv-2603-25848: Libralato and co-authors release the official catalogs of the Hubble Missing Globular Cluster Survey. The survey used Hubble to image 34 Galactic globular clusters never seen by it before. The catalogs give astro-photometric data for all of those clusters. The team describes its reduction steps and its photometric calibration. A link with the Gaia catalog keeps the photometry uniform. Artificial-star tests let users judge completeness and systematics. Merging Hubble and Gaia data sharpens absolute proper motions about threefold.
arxiv-2603-26648: He and co-authors introduce Vision2Web, a benchmark for building websites from visual designs with coding agents. The tasks scale from static page copying to interactive multi-page sites and full-stack builds. The set holds 193 tasks in 16 groups, drawn from real websites, with 918 prototype images and 1,255 test cases. Scoring pairs a GUI agent verifier with a vision-language judge under a workflow-based scheme. Even leading models show wide gaps at every level, and full-stack work still defeats them often.
arxiv-2603-26948: De Santis and co-authors present a compliance-aware take on predictive process monitoring. Standard predictors learn from event features alone and ignore process rules. A surgery, for example, may only be scheduled after a set waiting period. Their neuro-symbolic pipeline runs through feature extraction, rule extraction, and knowledge base creation. Logic Tensor Networks then inject the rules into the predictive model. Across all compliance-aware experiments, the model beat baseline predictors. It also followed the process constraints more closely while gaining accuracy.
arxiv-2603-27148: Dhodapkar and Pishori present SafetyDrift, a system that predicts when an AI agent's actions will turn unsafe. Single steps can look harmless while the sequence leaks data or breaks rules. SafetyDrift models agent trajectories as absorbing Markov chains over risk states. Closed-form absorption math gives the chance of a violation within a set horizon. Across 357 traces, points of no return varied sharply by task type. Communication tasks turned dangerous fast, unlike technical ones. Their monitor caught 94.7 percent of violations with 3.7 steps of warning.
arxiv-2603-28048: Yamaoka, Uchida, and Toyota extend score-based data assimilation, a diffusion-model method for inferring hidden states from time series. The standard method fails when the state's motion depends on unknown parameters that must be learned too. Their fix borrows self-organization, a classic trick for joint estimation, and folds it into the modern method. Tests on neuroscience and weather systems, plus a huge Kolmogorov flow, show the joint inference works and scales.
arxiv-2603-28248: Johansson frames reasoning as sliding downhill on a learned energy surface over a planned latent path. Single-shot decoders never revise, and chain-of-thought gives no score for progress. His EBRM model lowers an energy built from step fit, transition sense, and path smoothness. On graph and logic tasks the energy falls in a structured way. On a logic test, though, planning cut accuracy from 95% to 56%, a flaw he traces to drift and answers with anchoring fixes.
arxiv-2603-28948: Dolinsky and Zhang study scaling limits for exponential hedging in trinomial models that tend to the Black-Scholes model. They look at certainty equivalent prices for path dependent European options. As trading dates grow and risk aversion is scaled in step, a nontrivial limit appears. Their analysis is purely probabilistic, using duality, martingale tools, and weak convergence. The limit takes the form of a volatility control problem with a specific penalty. For Markovian payoffs, the delta hedging strategy is asymptotically optimal for the primal problem.
arxiv-2603-29448: Vicente examines how flavor deconstruction affects neutrinos. Flavor deconstruction gives each fermion family its own gauge group inside a larger symmetry. It is one tentative answer to the flavor puzzle. Neutrinos pose special challenges in such theories. Vicente reviews existing ideas in the literature. He then presents a simple model of his own. In the model, deconstruction leads naturally to sequential dominance. That pattern covers both neutrinos and charged leptons. It offers a workable account of lepton flavor structure.
arxiv-2603-29948: Shibasaki, Mohri, and Tsuchimochi propose TDΔSCF for electronic states that sit near degeneracy. Standard density functional methods struggle with such states. Their scheme starts from a non-Aufbau ΔSCF reference determinant. A time-dependent step then builds response states on that excited base. Unlike spin-flip variants, it keeps the usual Coulomb and exchange-correlation response terms. Tests cover ethylene twisting, diradical gaps, and benzyne shapes. Results show weaker functional dependence and smoother curves. Singlet energies tend to run high, they note.
arxiv-2604-00248: Taechoyotin and Acuna introduce REM-CTX, a reinforcement-learning review system that adds auxiliary context, such as figures and outside research signals, to manuscript text. It trains an 8-billion-parameter model with group relative policy optimization, pairing a quality reward spanning several aspects with two correspondence rewards that tie reviews to that context. Across computing, life, and physical science papers, it posts the highest quality among six baselines, beating larger commercial systems. Ablation tests show the two rewards complement each other, while criticism scores move against other metrics during training.
arxiv-2604-00348: Hakim and Agrawal propose making gray swans, plausible unobserved extremes, from the observational record, via gradient descent with a differentiable model. Minimizing the loss yields perturbed initial conditions giving a measurable outcome under size constraints. They turn Hurricane Fiona (2022) into a Sandy outcome: a Sandy track, warm core, and minimum pressure over 20 hPa lower than Sandy's. Extratropical perturbations matter more than hurricane ones, driving merger of a trough and the hurricane. Four Atlantic hurricanes yield swans, though the core goes unresolved and probability stays unknown.
arxiv-2604-00448: Brand, Gay, and Licata examine Morse diagrams under the connect sum of open books. A diagram of this kind codes a mapping class on a surface with boundary. It also fixes an open book decomposition of a three-dimensional manifold, and with it a contact structure. The paper looks closely at negative stabilisation and extracts a diagram test for overtwisted contact structures. When the open book pages are one-holed tori, the authors sort all diagrams that belong to one fixed decomposition.
arxiv-2604-00848: Benjamin Smith reviews and replicates a debiased estimator for many-variable regression by Javanmard and Montanari, where penalized fits like the LASSO add bias. The debiased fit restores a normal limit shape, so tests and intervals built from it are valid. He reruns part of the original simulations and real-data work, adding the desparsified LASSO, and finds good coverage and Type I error control. The projection fit wins power when signals are weak, while the original method holds up better when variables correlate in complex ways.
arxiv-2604-00948: Zhai and team develop a meshfree physics-guided neural network method for two-phase flow with moving edges, where two non-mixing fluids with different traits meet at a shifting edge. They address set edge motion, with speed plainly given, and flow-driven motion, set by the flow's speed field. Patched deep networks and space-time sampling in each zone power the method. The framework recasts the problem as a least-squares fit over rule, edge, and initial gaps, with strict estimate analysis via the Reynolds transport theorem.
arxiv-2604-01148: Saha and colleagues present BugScribe, a language-model approach linking user bug reports with app execution data to infer accurate observed behavior, expected behavior and steps to reproduce. A component-specific grounding strategy gives the model the context per report part, guided by a quality model. Tested on 48 bug reports from 26 Android apps with built ground truth, BugScribe beats the original reports and three language-model baselines. It improves steps-to-reproduce quality by 44 to 82 percent and observed/expected behavior quality by 4 to 35 percent.
arxiv-2604-01248: Ji and Piasecki trace the origin of the covariant Wigner operator as a quantum amplitude in QCD. The Wigner function encodes links among quarks, antiquarks, and gluons, yet its meaning stays subtle because of its quasiprobabilistic nature and negativity. Building on a Koopman-von Neumann-Sudarshan Hilbert space view of classical mechanics, they build a Koopman account of the quark Wigner operator. The operator proves isomorphic to a phase space spinor, so the Wigner function keeps its amplitude reading even relativistically and clarifies negativity and parton functions.
arxiv-2604-01348: Wu and colleagues argue that reasoning models waste know-how buried in past solution traces, which record how to reframe a problem, pick an approach and check or backtrack. Their Reasoning Memory system chops trajectories into subquestion-and-subroutine pairs, building a store of 32 million procedural entries. At test time the model states its subquestion and pulls matching subroutines inside its reasoning trace, reasoning under those priors. Across six math, science and coding benchmarks it beats document, trajectory and template retrieval, improving over no retrieval by 19.5 percent.
arxiv-2604-01948: Tagani, Fakhredine and Autieri chart how a field switches on quantum anomalous Hall conduction in a d-wave altermagnet on a Lieb lattice. Altermagnetic order splits spins by momentum without net magnetization, giving spin bands at X and Y valleys. The field breaks valley symmetry at zero total magnetization, so each valley shapes topology, with Chern numbers set by field and bandwidth. Berry curvature analysis finds gapped phases with total Chern numbers plus or minus 1, split by gap closings in valleys, offering fast magnetic control near the semimetal phase.
arxiv-2604-02048: Sugiura and colleagues build Jagle, the largest Japanese multimodal post training set, with about 9.2 million instances. English sets aggregate pools, but that path fails there, where sets are limited in scale and coverage. Instead the team gathers data and generates pairs through generation, translation and rendering. A model at 2.2B scale trained with Jagle beats InternVL3.5-2B on ten Japanese tasks, no more than five points from Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct. Combining Jagle with FineVision lifts English scores over FineVision.
arxiv-2604-02248: Kar and colleagues predict survival risk from data held by separate parties without pooling it. Their Bayesian vertical federated frame lets each client model one data type with a Bayesian neural net while a server merges mid level features. Privacy noise on client features guards against leaks during training. Against single type and pooled baselines it lifts ranking by up to 0.02 in C-index, staying robust under strict privacy budgets while reporting uncertainty.
arxiv-2604-02448: Dey and team review fundus image sets for diabetes eye care with a data centric lens. Auto finding and grading with deep learning can ease doctor burden but suffers scarce, narrow, uneven labeled sets. The review tests sets across binary sorting, stage grading, lesion finding and multi disease screening, and sorts them by size, access and label type. A recent dataset case study shows broader building issues, and the review flags missing standard lesion labels and over time data, with advice for future sets.
arxiv-2604-02548: Shahzad and four colleagues build a dataset of vulnerable code examples tied to CAPEC attack patterns and CWE weakness descriptions, a resource current datasets lack. They generate the snippets with GPT-4o, Llama and Claude models, and the three models agree closely, with codes at 0.98 cosine similarity. The final set holds 615 CAPEC snippets in Java, Python and JavaScript for training vulnerability detectors.
arxiv-2604-02848: Hasegawa, Kanai and Oki study when multinorm one tori, geometric objects tied to finite étale algebras, count as rational. Results hinge on d, the greatest common divisor of the degrees of the factors. The tori are stably rational for d equal to 1, and the team gives a criterion for retract rationality drawn from earlier work. For d above 1, they give conditions under which retract rationality fails. They also extend Endo-Miyata and Endo results to tori splitting over Galois extensions whose Sylow subgroups are cyclic, and over dihedral extensions.
arxiv-2604-03048: Neumüller and three colleagues test whether mixing language models with static code analysis improves automated algorithm spotting in source code. The team compares combined and standalone methods across prompting strategies, filter patterns, and systematic name obfuscation. Mixing models with lightweight static analysis cuts required model calls by 72 to 98 percent, while lifting F1-scores by up to 12 percentage points. In-context learning with two examples balances results and runtime at F1-scores of 75 to 77 percent. Models still identify most programs when names are obfuscated.
arxiv-2604-03448: Tang and colleagues offer ExpressEdit, a free Photoshop plugin that edits stylized face expressions without the global noise and pixel drift of other AI tools. It changes one within 3 seconds on one home graphics card and works with native tools like Liquify. A set of 135 tags with stories and images supports retrieval-based story work.
arxiv-2604-03848: Ahmed Bchatnia and team studied blow-up for a 1D damped nonlinear wave equation with derivative nonlinearity and scale-invariant damping. For large smooth starting data, they proved the blow-up curve has a well-defined slope everywhere. A key step mapped the blow-up shape. The proof turns the wave into a first-order system, using the Sasaki take on the Caffarelli-Friedman method for cases with time-derivative terms.
arxiv-2604-04248: Floricel, Plosker and Sadikov build distance rules for completely bounded maps between operator algebras. Their Bures-Kuratowski metrics stretch the Bures metric from completely positive maps to the wider class, using a Kuratowski embedding based at one map plus a coordinate from regular models. Each metric splits the space into the Bures cone and an outside part, joined at the anchor. The authors then study Vietoris-Rips and Čech complexes of these spaces. They give tests for mixed simplices; the mixed shape follows from the two part metrics.
arxiv-2604-04648: Yu, Wu and Block tackle reward hacking in best-of-N sampling, where N responses are scored and the best is picked. Performance can fall as N grows, because selection favors responses exploiting reward flaws. Their approach, called caution, reverses curiosity: curiosity rewards prediction error as novelty, while caution penalizes it. The authors explore pessimism, using lower confidence bounds to avoid uncertain out-of-distribution actions. Caution trains an error model on typical responses and lowers atypical estimates. Tests show caution mitigates reward hacking in best-of-N sampling.
arxiv-2604-04748: Shang, Yu and Chen present RegGuard, a framework that adds rule-based legitimacy checks to optimistic rollups for regulated finance. It pairs a rule language, RegSpec, that codes regulatory limits in a form a machine can decide, with a check that spots mismatched state between layers one and two. A third part orders trades in a checkable crypto way, with a tiny breach chance. A 15,000-line prototype built on Optimism cuts failed settlements by over 90 percent, blocks spotted order rigging, and keeps 85 percent of base speed.
arxiv-2604-04848: Bürger extends an earlier result on survival chances in supercritical Galton-Watson processes, branching models used in population genetics. The addendum proves that a fractional linear lower bound for the negative binomial generating function, proved earlier only up to the extinction probability, holds for every value between zero and one. That wider range closes a gap in Theorem 4.6 of the 2026 Journal of Mathematical Biology paper, making the bound usable across the full interval.
arxiv-2604-05248: Goyal and three colleagues present a line to refit models with memory modules, giving learning on hardware. Standard methods like full tuning face fatal loss, as changing dense codes causes clash across tasks. Sparse Memory Tuning pins updates to a subset of knobs in open memory layers. They extend with slot choice based on Kullback-Leibler gap, picking odd-token updates against a background spread. Refit models acquire new knowledge with loss of held-out skills, proving sparse updates in practice.
arxiv-2604-05448: Teng and Choo study how foreign domestic workers in Singapore use a language-model chatbot for daily, non-clinical emotional support. Caregiving strain, language gaps, and isolation weigh on these workers. Interviews and guided chats point to three themes. The bot felt safe and validating, it coped with broken language, and workers reused it for reassurance, guidance, and company. The authors draw design lessons around safety, access, and flexible use.
arxiv-2604-05848: Park and four colleagues judge learner profiles for tutoring AI without waiting for lesson results. Their distinctiveness score rates how each learner stands apart from cohort peers by pairwise distance, needing no clusters, labels, or task tests. Learner-level profiles split students better than interaction-level ones, giving a handy pre-deployment check.
arxiv-2604-06448: Madabhushi and five colleagues build a graph-based anomaly detector for Prime Video microservices, linked services behind video streams. Load tests mimic spikes from Thursday Night Football and Rings of Power, yet miss quirks seen only in real traffic. Their system learns node-level graph embeddings from directed service graphs with a GCN-GAE model, flagging gaps between load-test and event embeddings. It spots incident services, and a synthetic injection test reports 96 percent precision, false positives under a tenth of a percent, and recall of 58 percent.
arxiv-2604-06648: The Euclid Collaboration presents an end-to-end pipeline for finding strong galaxy-galaxy lensing systems in Euclid's first quick data release. Starting from VIS catalogs, the pipeline drops point sources, cuts deflectors by magnitude, and filters artifacts into small image cutouts. A seed classifier plus morphology-balanced negatives trains a modified VGG16 model, refined over three rounds. Human grading of the top 4,000 candidates yields 441 Grade A or B systems, including 130 new ones, while the model recovers 740 of 905 known candidates in its top 20,000 predictions.
arxiv-2604-06848: Klurman and Mangerel prove a sharp mean value formula for bounded multiplicative functions and draw out several long sought gains. Their formula sharpens a twenty year old bound of Granville and Soundararajan for fully multiplicative signs, giving a firm floor for a weighted sum that falls slowly with size. When the function does not mimic the Liouville sign pattern, the fall rate can be pushed near the best possible pace. For a random sign function, they show the chance the sum dips below zero shrinks fast.
arxiv-2604-06948: Gholami tackles nonstationary wavelet phase gauging with tuned fitting. Seismic wavelet phase drifts in space and time from fading, spread, and tuning. Raising kurtosis and skewness pushes signals toward non-Gaussian or uneven zero-phase states, but window methods prove unstable. Gholami casts the task as tuned fitting solved by ADMM. He derives the first closed-form nearness tools for inverse kurtosis and skewness. Signed swaps reduce tasks to 1D root-finding, and tests on fake and real data show linear cost and calm.
arxiv-2604-07448: Paganelli and four colleagues ask when randomization helps Hamiltonian simulation. Their sparse-QSVT method treats large terms exactly and samples small terms at random, tracking error growth through block-encoding and QSVT steps. On random Hamiltonians built to favor randomization, gate counts fall up to tenfold for many-term, uneven cases. The edge holds only at moderate precision: near an error of ten to the minus three, deterministic methods win, and real chemistry structure likely favors them more.
arxiv-2604-07548: Munira and Manikonda analyze 210840 Google Play reviews of Character AI, tying each review to the app version live at posting. Ratings fluctuate across versions, with certain versions drawing stronger bad ratings. Theme analysis finds complaints cluster on tech glitches and errors, while a subset of reviews frames concerns in mental-health or habit-related terms. The findings show how overall ratings and voiced concerns vary across software rounds, showing the value of steady behavior and clear talk in changing AI apps.
arxiv-2604-07648: Mota investigates vacuum current density for a scalar field in dispiration spacetime threaded by flux. The background joins a cosmic string and a screw dislocation, giving a twisted geometry. From Klein-Gordon mode functions, the author evaluates the Wightman function for the current density. Beyond the azimuthal component of current around the defect, a nonzero axial component is induced by the structure. Both components are periodic in flux, depending only on its fraction. The screw dislocation regularizes the axial component at the origin and sets its size.
arxiv-2604-07848: Zhang and Cheng uncover a hidden assumption behind gradient-based task analysis in multi-task learning. Joint training sometimes helps a lot and sometimes actively harms, with no principled way to predict which. They show gradient conflicts reveal genuine task relationships only when tasks share training instances. Measured on disjoint inputs, apparent signals mix task relationships with distributional shift. The sample-overlap requirement turns sharply: below 30 percent overlap, gradient-task correlations look like noise, while above 40 percent they reliably recover known structure.
arxiv-2604-07948: Sipacheva proves that every countable-dimensional topological vector space over a suitable field has a closed discrete basis. The field may be a complete nondiscrete second-countable valued field, such as the real or complex numbers, or a finite field. The result gives a clean structural guarantee: however large the countable dimension, a basis can be chosen that is both closed and discrete. That combination matters because closed discrete sets behave well under topological operations. The short proof settles the existence question for this whole class of spaces.
arxiv-2604-08148: Kuntur and four colleagues offer a lightweight hybrid approach to clickbait detection using OpenAI semantic embeddings with six compact heuristic cues for style and information. To improve speed, vectors are reduced using PCA and tested with XGBoost, GraphSAGE, and GCN models. While simple feature design yields slightly lower F1-scores, graph models achieve competitive performance with much reduced run time. High ROC-AUC values further indicate strong discrimination power, supporting reliable spotting of clickbait headlines under varying decision thresholds.
arxiv-2604-08248: Ziampras, Qiao, and Haworth study parts in outside-lit protoplanetary disks: spirals and rings in 2D flows. Light from nearby massive stars can strip mass from such disks and shape their growth, but its motion impact on the disks is new in detail. They aim to study how uneven outside irradiation shapes the structure of such disks. They run 2D multi-fluid light hydrodynamics models of such disks under external irradiation with the PLUTO code, treating it as a flat flux with a simple heating rate.
arxiv-2604-08348: Illesca and three colleagues study SMC star cluster kinematics, using residual motions to disentangle perturbations. The SMC's motion behaviour remains challenging, tackled diversely by many authors. Observational evidence has grown for tidal perturbations from the Large Magellanic Cloud on the SMC, especially outward. Star clusters serve as kinematic tracers of the SMC. They analyse 36 clusters across regions: Northern Bridge, Southern Bridge, Wing/Bridge, West Halo, Main Body, and Counter-Bridge. From proper motions, radial velocity, and distance per cluster, they estimate Cartesian velocities in the SMC frame.
arxiv-2604-08448: Wanzare and sixteen colleagues release AfriVoices-KE, a speech dataset of about 3,000 hours across five Kenyan languages: Dholuo, Kikuyu, Kalenjin, Maasai, and Somali. Recordings from 4,777 native speakers mix 750 scripted hours with 2,250 hours of spontaneous speech, gathered by phone app across varied regions. Layered checks on sound quality and content accuracy support speech recognition and synthesis work for languages long left out of speech technology.
arxiv-2604-08648: Mishra-Sharma and three colleagues bring differentiable probabilistic programming to the gamma ray sky, targeting the long standing Galactic Center excess puzzle. Their differentiable forward model and likelihood use GPU acceleration to weigh a continuum of spatial shapes for the excess in one probabilistic fit, with variational inference over the large model space. Beyond gamma rays, the work showcases the method as a flexible tool for astrophysical data analysis.
arxiv-2604-08748: Abe and colleagues test Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory plans for chasing GeV to TeV signals. Their target is binary neutron star mergers in observing run O5. Using mock merger samples with gravity wave finds and model based short gamma ray burst output, including off axis jets, they model observations with device response, sky tiling, and varying skies. A tuned plan makes about 5 percent of mock gravity wave linked short bursts seen, with jet and viewing angles driving whether they are seen.
arxiv-2604-08948: Hu and seven colleagues introduce TaxPraBen, the first benchmark built for language models doing realistic Chinese tax work rather than isolated language tasks. It combines ten standard application tasks with practical exercises graded against Bloom's taxonomy of learning levels. The field is knowledge-heavy and rule-bound, and general models show clear gaps there. Tests of 19 models find large gaps in scores: big closed-source models lead, Chinese models such as Qwen2.5 generally beat rivals in other languages, and a tax-tuned model improves only modestly.
arxiv-2604-09248: Sambale, Schulte, and Thaele study limit laws for the longest edges in empty region graphs. In such graphs, vertices are points, and an edge joins a pair when an associated region holds no other vertices. For graphs from a stationary Poisson process, they let intensity tend to infinity and track edge midpoints, transformed lengths, and directions. They prove the transformed process converges to a Poisson process, and the longest edge length in a window converges to a Gumbel variable, with explicit error bounds.
arxiv-2604-09648: Islam and five colleagues present TRACE, the first framework measuring exhaled carbon dioxide from free-roaming cattle by thermal video. No current system gives continuous, spatially resolved readings without touching the animals. TRACE segments carbon-dioxide plumes per frame and classifies emission flux per clip from mid-wave infrared footage. Gas-aware attention and temporal fusion capture breath-cycle dynamics. Against fifteen leading models on a farm thermal-gas dataset, it scores 0.998 mean intersection over union and tops every metric at once.
arxiv-2604-09848: Rosa da Silva and Rossi study two local-nonlocal systems on a domain split A and B. First, a local parabolic equation in A pairs with a nonlocal elliptic balance in B; then roles reverse. A nonlocal kernel moves mass across the interface, with Neumann boundary conditions in both. The authors prove solutions exist and are unique, show total mass is preserved and the parabolic part decays toward a constant elliptic solution. The coupled problem is also the limit of a purely parabolic problem as one component slows to zero.
arxiv-2604-09948: Zhu and Xu present a split-guided spatial-spectral Mamba for many-band image sorting, tackling mixed spectra and fragile edges. A spectral split network learns pure pixels and spread maps, handling pure-pixel shifts and splitting mixed pixels. Spread clusters drive tuned Top-K token picks for Mamba chains, and a split-guided Mamba module lifts token learning and order. A multi-task scheme learns pure-pixel-spread patterns and labels, giving sorting maps plus a spectral library. Tests on four sets show large gains over rivals.
arxiv-2604-10048: Raj, Jha, Anand, and Saha reframe conversational recommendation as structured decision-making. Most systems chase search scores or fluent replies instead of good recommendations. Their HARPO framework splits quality into relevance, diversity, satisfaction, and engagement, weighted by context. Tree-search reasoning guided by a learned value network then picks the best paths. Tests on ReDial, INSPIRED, and MUSE show steady gains in recommendation quality with strong reply quality.
arxiv-2604-10148: Randeep and Saha build a closed-form account of inflation with a derivative-coupled scalar field. In their model, gravity and the scalar field interact through the Ricci tensor times field derivatives. They estimate the scalar spectral index and tensor-to-scalar ratio for power-law, exponential alpha-attractor, Arctan, Hilltop, and polynomial potentials. Higher derivative terms from the coupling cause no singularity in slow-roll. For each potential set, the index and ratio values match ACT and Planck observations.
arxiv-2604-10248: Su and Fang model factory forecasts under shifting work conditions with a multi-head attention fusion network. Engines, turbines, and machines wear in their own ways as work shifts, making forecasts hard. Their method fuses three signal parts: a wear trend, discrete work states from grouping encoded as vectors, and leftover noise. BiLSTM networks capture time links, weighting time steps and sensor signals as needed. A fusion module joins the trend branch with state vectors to capture their links. Tests on a NASA data set confirm the method works.
arxiv-2604-10348: Gabarrete, Montoya, and Raudales derive the entropy vector field for a relativistic kinetic gas of free, spinless, massive, neutral bits on bound orbits in space-time. With dependence on orbit tilt, they model spinning and still gases around a Schwarzschild black hole. They analyze readings built from bit density, energy density, and main pushes, like the skew index and kinetic heat. Spinning and still cases differ sharply, most in far-out shape of skew, heat, and average pressure, showing angular spin in shaping free gases under strong gravity.
arxiv-2604-11148: Aksoy and two colleagues propose a compound integrated circuit protection system with light cryptography. Many methods protect integrated circuits from threats in the supply chain, such as excess and theft. Most prior methods are weak because they do not rely on proven secure rules. Earlier methods increase hardware cost and are open to removal and power attacks. The system uses a light cryptography method with logic locking and hardware obfuscation. Tests show secure designs from the tool have less hardware cost than earlier designs and resist existing attacks.
arxiv-2604-11248: Berdica and three colleagues evolve populations of Petri Dish neural cellular automata toward open-ended complexity. Standard systems collapse into frozen patterns or noise and depend heavily on settings, so their PBT-NCA algorithm rewards both past behavioral novelty and present visual diversity. The evolving substrate produces coordinated waves, spore-like clusters that colonize new ground, and shape-shifting structures with active interiors. This sustains complexity at the edge of chaos.
arxiv-2604-11448: Vergara studies p-variational capacity of condensers, where both plates come from one phase function via level sets. Restricting potentials to phase forms and applying the coarea formula reduces the problem to a level function. An energy weight governs it, combining phase gradient and level-set shape. He derives a formula for the reduced problem, builds an optimal profile, and bounds the capacity by fibered restriction. He bounds the energy weight, studies critical levels, and gives exact-reduction models, plus a tangential obstruction in the linear case.
arxiv-2604-11648: Coccaro, Schiavi, and Zaio present a hit filter to speed online track reconstruction at hadron colliders. Trigger systems must judge collision products fast, and rebuilding charged-particle paths in inner detectors is combinatorial, with run time growing with pile-up. The High-Luminosity LHC upgrade will raise hit counts and swell costs. Their convolutional-neural-network filter drops unneeded detector data and runs easily on accelerator cards. The paper covers the filter, weighs its impact, and discusses next steps.
arxiv-2604-11748: Chen and six colleagues present LangFlow, the continuous diffusion model matching discrete diffusion. Continuous diffusion excels at fast images, but prior language models lagged discrete rivals given sparse data. LangFlow links embedding diffusion models to Flow Matching via Bregman divergence. Its innovations are an ODE-based NLL bound, an information-uniform noise schedule motivating a tuned Gumbel scheduler, and revised training with self-conditioning. LangFlow rivals discrete models on perplexity measures, reaching 30.0 on LM1B and 24.6 on OpenWebText, and beats autoregressive baselines on 4 of 7 zero-shot benchmarks.
arxiv-2604-11948: Shen and five colleagues propose AILFM, an active imitation learning scheduler for large foundation model inference on 3D-stacked static non-uniform cache many-cores. Such systems offer bandwidth and locality but suffer severe thermal problems and uneven cache latencies from 3D networks-on-chip. Thread migration and voltage-frequency scaling face kernel diversity and system heterogeneity. AILFM learns near-optimal thermal-aware policies from Oracle demonstrations with minimal run-time overhead, accounting for core and kernel differences, and beating state-of-the-art baselines across diverse workloads.
arxiv-2604-12348: Goswami and two colleagues present PrivEraserVerify, one system for federated unlearning that joins speed, privacy, and a way to prove removal. Adaptive checkpointing keeps key past updates for fast rebuilding, layer-wise differentially private calibration removes a departing client's influence with little accuracy loss, and fingerprint checks let participants confirm removal without central control. Tests on image, handwriting, and medical data show removal two to three times faster than retraining.
arxiv-2604-12848: Yannis Voet and three colleagues fix bad systems in immersed finite element methods. Trimming in design tools merges or drops shape parts, creating tiny cut pieces. Tiny cut pieces wreck matrix health, needing fixes. The paper first sizes up the scaled matrix and shows where standard fixes fail. A robust deflation fix tailored to immersed methods is then put forth.
arxiv-2604-13348: Srivastava and three colleagues present CONCORD, a setup in which assistants that listen all the time work together without sharing raw speech. Only the owner's voice is kept, checked by speaker verification, leaving a one-sided transcript that guards privacy but leaves gaps. CONCORD fills needed gaps with place-and-time clues, gap detection, and short queries between assistants, limited by how the speakers relate. On a dialogue dataset across many domains it reaches about 91 percent recall in gap detection, 96 percent relationship accuracy, and 97 percent true negatives on sensitive disclosures.
arxiv-2604-13748: Ma and three colleagues forecast many series over time, where each series behaves differently. One model for all can miss the differences. A model per series can go wrong. Their framework groups series by out-of-sample predictive performance, not by similar representations. Assignments update from validation losses for point and probabilistic forecasts. A fallback returns to the global model when specialization fails to help. Traffic tests show gains without degradation when differences are weak.
arxiv-2604-13948: Xiao-Jing Gao, Yanfeng Ge, and Yan Gao propose a boron crystal, P63-B30, where a two-dimensional nodal surface coexists with several kinds of Weyl fermions. Time-reversal plus screw symmetry pins the nodal surface to one plane, while rotational symmetries protect double, type-I, and type-II Weyl points. Wide separation between surface and points lets each be resolved on its own, and surface states show Fermi arcs linking nodes of opposite chirality.
arxiv-2604-14048: Dai and Yang let feed-forward 3D reconstruction models improve themselves at test time without ground truth. Free Geometry masks some frames to build a self-supervised task, enforcing cross-view feature consistency between full and partial observations while preserving relations implied by held-out frames. Lightweight LoRA updates recalibrate a model in under 2 minutes per dataset, lifting camera pose accuracy by 3.73 percent and point-map prediction by nearly 3 percent.
arxiv-2604-14348: Liao studies how transit access shapes who shares city venues, using phone location data from nine Swedish cities and three American ones. Places draw a mix of visitors, measured by the birth backgrounds of their home areas, and transit catchment mix predicts visitor mix. The link holds only in the biggest metro areas; in smaller Swedish cities it fades once centrality, venue density, and catchment makeup are held fixed. Transit-diversity hotspots sit not in mixed venues but in quieter, less commercial spots with few other paths to mix.
arxiv-2604-14448: Almeida and eight colleagues present MARCA, a bilingual English-Portuguese benchmark for testing language models on web-based information seeking. Fifty-two hand-written multi-entity questions pair with hand-checked checklist rubrics that score answer completeness and correctness. Fourteen models run under two setups: a basic path with direct search and scraping, and an orchestrator path that splits tasks across delegated subagents. Orchestration often improves coverage, scores vary widely across models, and transfer between English and Portuguese proves uneven.
arxiv-2604-14848: Remlein, Esposito, and Avanzini ask when open reaction network behavior emerges from closed ones. Open networks model out-of-equilibrium chemistry via chemostats exchanging species, yet finite systems relax to equilibrium. Open-network behavior arises from closed networks under two conditions: fast reactions as exchanges, and abundant species acting as chemostats. Here, stochastic dynamics and thermodynamic structure, including entropy production and free-energy balance, emerge to leading order. The regime lasts up to a time proportional to the abundance scale, giving a test of how long closed systems act open.
arxiv-2604-14948: Berti, Polimeni, and Terracini study outward N-body paths driven by homogeneous Newton fields. Half-entire outward motions exist with given setup and course for many powers. Their approach minimizes a tuned action, treating hyperbolic, parabolic, and hyperbolic-parabolic regimes jointly. They derive refined series with higher fixes, lifting growth bounds. For hyperbolic-parabolic paths, linear cluster-center escape meets internal parabolic motion, stretching cluster spreading to general fields.
arxiv-2604-15048: Ahmed and four others propose GAT-QNN, a genetic framework for hybrid quantum neural networks. Hybrid networks combine classical learning with quantum circuits, but NISQ noise and large design spaces limit performance. GAT-QNN trains a macroCircuit by sampling microCircuits, reintegrating their parameters. After training, a genetic inference stage evaluates microCircuits with macroCircuit weights and selects top architectures. Backend-aware selection needs no retraining and can cut gates. On four-class MNIST, genetic inference gains 22 to 23 percent accuracy across backends.
arxiv-2604-15148: Liang and colleagues sharpen search-augmented reasoning with IG-Search, a framework that rewards each search step by information gain. For every step, the gain measures how much retrieved pages raise confidence in the gold answer versus random pages, judging the query itself. That signal flows back to query tokens through per-token advantage modulation in GRPO. Across seven question-answering benchmarks the method beats the strongest trajectory-level baseline by 1.6 points, and it still learns when every sampled trajectory fails.
arxiv-2604-15448: Pal and Kadioglu ask whether pre-trained embeddings built for mixed-integer programming can transfer to Boolean satisfiability. Mapping CNF formulas onto the same bipartite constraint-variable graphs lets them reuse the model with no design change or labeled fine-tuning. The vectors capture SAT structure well enough for unsupervised grouping and distribution spotting, a first step toward one shared code for optimization and decision problems.
arxiv-2604-15848: Mikkelsen and three colleagues present a phase-only time-reversal method for steering photonic nanojets, tight beams of light, without moving parts or amplitude control. A source placed at the target spot defines a phase pattern for a control line, fit for a spatial light modulator, that shapes the desired jet. Full-wave simulations show robust lateral and axial steering with tight subwavelength focus and low sidelobes. The design also survives moderate shape, making, and alignment errors.
arxiv-2604-16348: Hausladen and five co-authors study spatial anchoring and LLM agents for public planning, in an experiment with 200 participants. People learned about a green project from a street redesign, through text and images, or through narrated 360-degree video with spatial audio. They then engaged with LLM personas. The video condition improved recall and changed replies. They named winners more often, asked more project questions, and gave more positive feedback. The authors offer a framing of LLMs as dialogue partners, causal evidence, and a test method for cities.
arxiv-2604-16748: Ao proposes TriTS, a cross-modal framework projecting time series into time, frequency and two-dimensional vision spaces. Long-term forecasting struggles because real signals carry entangled dynamics that a purely one-dimensional view misses. Period-Aware Reshaping plus Visual Mamba bridges the gap at linear cost, modelling cross-period links as textures. A Multi-Resolution Wavelet Mixing module splits non-stationary signals into trend and noise for time-frequency localization. A streaming linear branch anchors stability, and fusion lets TriTS adapt across contexts with state-of-the-art results.
arxiv-2604-16848: Cui and colleagues open Tower, a benchmark for transmission-corridor point cloud cutting. Fine-grained cutting of corridor point clouds backs power-line checks, but data lack and long scenes limit progress. The dataset holds 661 scenes and two point four six six billion points, with a 22-class list and set splits. A global-local fusion framework joins a whole-scene branch capturing long-range topology with a local branch retaining fine geometry. Fused predictions pass geometric validation, and experiments show the benchmark's challenge and the framework's robustness.
arxiv-2604-17248: Lin and three colleagues propose VIBE, a framework for evaluating generative bias in large audio models through open tasks with human speech. Existing speech fairness benchmarks rely on synthetic speech and choice questions, giving only a fragmented view of fairness. Open tasks such as personalized recommendations let stereotypical associations surface without preset options and extend easily to new tasks. Testing 12 top models reveals systematic biases in realistic scenarios: both gender and accent cues trigger statistically significant distributional shifts, and bias magnitude depends strongly on the task.
arxiv-2604-17348: Yuliia Samoilenko and Valerii Samoilenko build soliton-like and peakon-like solutions of the Camassa-Holm equation with varying coefficients and small dispersion. Each solution pairs a shared regular background with a singular part carrying their own features, with the main singular term defined. In the one-phase case that term is pinned down and higher corrections are shown solvable, giving solutions as close as desired in the small parameter. Two-phase solutions are also built, with accuracy theorems and examples shown as graphs.
arxiv-2604-17448: Kumar and four colleagues introduce AVICA, a fully automated pipeline for calibrating big VLBI radio-telescope data sets in CASA. Data from the Very Long Baseline Array span three decades of formats, and the SMILE project alone needs some 5,000 sources done. AVICA automates prep work, choice of calibrator and antenna by fringe detection, and the full workflow, tracked live by its ALFRD system. Tested on 1,000 archival sources, it finished 978 of them in about 30 minutes each, proving blind calibration at scale.
arxiv-2604-17648: Olabisi, Mitra, and Agrawal introduce ThreadSumm, a multi-stage framework for summing up deeply nested threads, where tangled replies, quotes, and mixed topics defeat standard tools. The method first plans content by pulling discourse aspects and Atomic Content Units, then orders lines into thread-aware chains showing multiple views rather than one linear strand. A Tree of Thoughts search then drafts and scores multiple passage options, jointly tuning flow and breadth. The design yields summaries with clear logic beating current rivals.
arxiv-2604-17848: Hamada and Misumi test whether the confined phase of a large-N gauge theory with one adjoint Dirac fermion survives shrinking one spatial direction. They use a partially reduced twisted Eguchi-Kawai model on a small lattice, tracking the Polyakov loop and order parameters for volume independence. At N equal to 36 with periodic boundaries, the loop stays near zero for light fermions as the circle shrinks, supporting adiabatic continuity between large and small circles. With antiperiodic boundaries, by contrast, the loop shows a clear deconfinement transition.
arxiv-2604-18048: Díaz and nineteen colleagues present the first X-ray polarization results for the atoll source 4U 1735-44 from joint IXPE, NICER, and NuSTAR observations. Over 2 to 8 kilo-electronvolts they find a weak polarization signal of 1.4 percent at an angle of minus 29 degrees, with an upper limit at three sigma of 3.5 percent. The best-fit spectrum mixes disk heat, a Comptonized blackbody, and reflection. From reflection they infer a disk inclination near 40 degrees, like other atoll sources, where low tilt likely explains the weak signal.
arxiv-2604-18548: Lavery and five colleagues extend bio-informed networks to 2D-plus-time systems for equation learning. These networks preserve known operator structure, such as reaction-diffusion, while learning inner terms via trainable subnets held by soft costs. Current studies cover only 1D-plus-time systems and forward runs, treating the ruling law as a smoother, not an ID target. The new method joins data cleaning, law learning, and symbolic regression for finding. Shown on lung cancer cell growth from time-lapse imaging, it finds 2D-plus-time models.
arxiv-2604-18848: Continelli, Haskovec, and Pignotti investigate consensus and flocking in multi agent systems with two delays. A transmission delay covers information exchange between agents, while a reaction delay covers processing time before agents adjust their states. For a simple linear two agent system, they show explicitly how delays affect asymptotic stability. They derive sufficient conditions for asymptotic consensus and flocking in the general multi agent setting with a nonlinear, globally positive influence function. The conditions require delays small relative to initial data and the decay rate of the influence function.
arxiv-2604-19148: Beaudin and six colleagues present a Gaussian process path planner for robotic exploration that adapts to multi-modal sensing data and respects state and input constraints. They optimize waypoints over receding horizons, with cost given by the Gaussian process posterior over waypoints. The method, called OLAhGP, is demonstrated on a surface vessel tracking algal blooms using model data and field sensing data. Simulated and field results show improvement over existing methods: with equal samples, it generates more informative paths and identifies blooms more accurately in chlorophyll rich waters.
arxiv-2604-19248: Iwai, Hikasa, and Okajima design vehicle path following that treats steering angle as a state driven by torque against resistance, rather than as a direct command. That resistance depends on the road surface and is hard to pin down, so its coefficient is treated as uncertain. A model error compensator feeds back the gap between the real vehicle and a parallel nominal model. Simulations show the maximum following error falling by more than 90 percent against the usual method.
arxiv-2604-19348: Francener and Goncalves examine the rare neutrino trident process, in which a hit yields two charged leptons, using two upcoming sites. They study the Scattering and Neutrino Detector at the Large Hadron Collider in its high-luminosity run, and give first numbers for the SHiP beam-dump experiment. The two sites probe different energy ranges. With new setups assumed, they estimate cross-sections for all possible leptonic final states in coherent and incoherent processes.
arxiv-2604-19448: Nauta, Gerhold, and Huisman advocate fuzzing as a practical way to improve deductive verifiers. As these tools mature, their users grow beyond core developers, so tools must run reliably, give clear error messages, and show correct results. Yet deductive verifiers are large, complex software, and fully verifying them is often out of reach. The paper shows how fuzz testing applies to them, demonstrated with AValAnCHE, a prototype linked to the VerCors verifier.
arxiv-2604-19848: Sertkan and Sakallı study charged scalar waves around the rotating Kerr-EMDA black hole, a solution of Einstein-Maxwell-Dilaton-Axion theory. From the gauge-covariant Klein-Gordon equation they separate variables and solve both parts exactly with confluent Heun functions. The resonant frequencies come out evenly spaced in their imaginary parts, with spacing fixed by the black hole mass alone. The same analysis yields an entropy quantum that simplifies for Schwarzschild but diverges at extremality, plus the first analytic greybody factor for this geometry.
arxiv-2604-20048: Zhao and five colleagues test whether large language models judge cities neutrally across cultures. Using a globally stratified street-view set, they prompt three frontier multimodal models for open descriptions and structured scores. The models' neutral baseline sits closer to European and North American framings than to others. Prompting can nudge outputs toward specific regional human views, but flattens demographic variety and adds sentiment-based self-favoring bias, warning against treating AI as a neutral urban judge.
arxiv-2604-20148: Kumar asks whether small language models can handle tool use well without complex adaptation tricks. He compares few-shot prompting with hypernetwork-generated LoRA weights on a 3B Llama model across four benchmarks. Few-shot examples add over 21 percent to performance and documentation adds about five percent, while the hypernetwork adds nothing despite its hundreds of millions of parameters. A well-prompted 3B model reaches 79.7 percent of GPT-5's average performance at ten times lower latency, steering practitioners toward prompt design and example curation.
arxiv-2604-20348: Palma and six colleagues present BiCICLe, a frame that lets plain language models run two-arm robot manipulation from a few examples, with no fine-tuning. Two-arm control splits into a leader-follower team task, with arm moves predicted one after another under tight coordination. On 13 tasks from the TWIN benchmark it hits 70.5 percent mean success, beating the best training-free baseline by about six points and topping most supervised methods. Real-world tests on 3 tasks confirm strong performance with no hardware-specific retraining.
arxiv-2604-20848: Mehta presents MATRAG, a framework joining multi-agent teamwork with knowledge-graph search to deliver clear recommendations. MATRAG employs four custom agents: a User Modeling Agent for taste sketches, and an Item Analysis Agent for semantic features from knowledge graphs. The Reasoning Agent merges signals, and an Explanation Agent writes reasons grounded in found knowledge. Tests on three sets (Amazon Reviews, MovieLens-1M, and Yelp) show that MATRAG hits state-of-the-art scores. It lifts pick quality by about 13 percent (Hit Rate) and about 15 percent (NDCG) over leading rivals.
arxiv-2604-20948: Truong and colleagues offer a virtual agent for wellbeing support that aims to feel personal and caring, not flat. It draws on trusted sources, keeps a structured memory of the user, and talks across more than one channel. Tests show it finds and frames replies better than plain language models, with the edge largest for small models. In a study with students in Vietnam and Australia, it topped language-model-only rivals on clarity, trust in its facts, and felt empathy, and most students picked it.
arxiv-2604-21148: Siyu Liang and Alicia Beckford Wassink interview speech-recognition users across four U.S. dialect regions to capture what error rates leave out. Participants say tools ignore their cultural backgrounds and demand constant adjustment, yet they still expect strong performance and want to help improve the models. The deeper cost is emotional labor: code-switching, over-enunciating, and managing frustration while blaming themselves for systems not built for them.
arxiv-2604-21348: Christopher Ewasiuk and Stefano Profumo prove a quantum conservation law for an oscillator coupled to a ghost degree of freedom, a wrong-sign term long feared to cause runaway. A second classical conserved quantity lifts to a quantum operator commuting with the Hamiltonian. It bounds the mean squared phase-space radius for all time and every state with finite second moments. Three numerical frameworks confirm confinement below the bound, a real spectrum, and Poisson level statistics. Ghost instability, they conclude, hinges on interaction structure, not the wrong sign.
arxiv-2604-21448: Bodhinanda Chandra, Sachith Dunatunga, and Ken Kamrin build one continuum model for rate-dependent granular flows across regimes. Two rate effects, micro-inertia and viscoelastic damping, sit inside one continuum picture, with a direct link from the restitution coefficient to continuum viscosity via wave attenuation. Viscous damping steers wave motion and collisions without changing the plastic flow rule. Built with the material point method, the model captures wave motion, diffusion, and rate-dependent behavior across steady, transient, shaking, and impact-driven flows.
arxiv-2604-21848: Wogan and seven colleagues argue that life detection on rocky exoplanets should infer surface gas fluxes, not just atmospheric abundances.
